prompts.display_text: Pin the Sao Paulo Brazil Temple, the first temple in South America.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Sao Paulo Brazil Temple, the first temple in South America.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple pages, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Ground was broken in March 1976, and President Spencer W. Kimball dedicated the temple from October 30 to November 2, 1978. It was the first temple in South America. The dedication came only months after the June 1978 revelation extending the priesthood to all worthy male members, which allowed many Brazilian Saints to enter.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Americas with a dedicated temple in a city that is not its capital.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the Americas with a dedicated temple named for a city that is not its capital (as of November 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Ten countries outside the Americas have temples named for non-capital cities. Australia is the clearest case: all five of its temples sit outside Canberra. Others include Preston England, Frankfurt and Freiberg Germany, The Hague, Hamilton New Zealand, Aba Nigeria and Abidjan Côte d'Ivoire (the capital is Yamoussoukro).

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Perth and Brisbane (capital: Canberra).

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Preston England (capital: London).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Fukuoka, Sapporo and Okinawa (capital: Tokyo).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Cebu City, Urdaneta, Davao and Bacolod (capital: Manila).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Freiberg and Frankfurt (capital: Berlin).

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Aba (capital: Abuja).

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Hamilton and Auckland (capital: Wellington).

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Johannesburg and Durban (capital: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein).

answers.name: Côte d'Ivoire
answers.fact: Abidjan (capital: Yamoussoukro).

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Hague (capital: Amsterdam).

prompts.display_text: Pin an African or Asian country where Swahili, Igbo, Yoruba, Xhosa, Tswana, Lingala, Khmer or Mongolian is official or national.
prompts.text_original: Between 2000 and 2009 the Church published first complete Book of Mormon editions in Swahili, Igbo, Yoruba, Xhosa, Tswana, Lingala, Khmer and Mongolian. Pin an African or Asian country where one of those eight languages is an official or national language of the country.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Kenya, DR Congo, Nigeria, South Africa, Cambodia, Mongolia
prompts.summary: The 2000s were a decade of African and Asian firsts. Swahili and Igbo editions came in 2000, Xhosa the same year, Mongolian and Khmer in 2001, Zulu and Tswana in 2003, Lingala in 2004 and Yoruba in 2007. Swahili alone serves members in Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda and the Congo.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: Igbo (2000) and Yoruba (2007) editions were published; both are national languages of Nigeria.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: Swahili (2000) and full Lingala (2004) editions; both are national languages.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: The Swahili Book of Mormon was published in September 2000; Swahili is official in Kenya.

answers.name: Mongolia
answers.fact: The Mongolian Book of Mormon was published in 2001.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Xhosa (2000), Zulu and Tswana (2003) editions were published.

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: The complete Khmer Book of Mormon was published in November 2001.

answers.name: Tanzania
answers.fact: Swahili, Tanzania's national language, received its Book of Mormon in 2000.

answers.name: Uganda
answers.fact: Swahili is an official language of Uganda; its Book of Mormon came in 2000.

answers.name: Botswana
answers.fact: Tswana, Botswana's national language, received its Book of Mormon in 2003.

answers.name: Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Lingala, a national language of the Republic of the Congo, got its full Book of Mormon in 2004.

answers.name: Rwanda
answers.fact: Swahili, given its Book of Mormon in 2000, is one of four official languages of Rwanda (since 2017).

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: Tswana and Xhosa, given Book of Mormon editions in 2003 and 2000, are among Zimbabwe's 16 official languages.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Middle East that got its first Church mission headquartered there between 1900 and 1939.
prompts.text_original: In the first four decades of the twentieth century the Church organized new missions with headquarters in countries that had never hosted one. Pin a country outside the Middle East that got its first Church mission headquartered there between 1900 and 1939.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Sweden, Tonga, Canada, Norway, Brazil, Japan, Argentina, Czech Republic (and facts page); Presidents of the Church Student Manual, chapter 7
prompts.summary: Between 1900 and 1939 the Church placed a first mission headquarters in Japan (1901), Sweden (1905), Tonga (1916), Canada (1919), Norway (1920), Argentina (1926), Czechoslovakia (about 1929) and Brazil (1935). Denmark is not an answer: the Scandinavian Mission had been headquartered in Copenhagen since 1850.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: The Brazilian Mission was organized in 1935, separating Brazil from the South American Mission.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: The South American Mission, headquartered in Buenos Aires, was established July 15, 1926, with Reinhold Stoof as president.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: The Canadian Mission, headquartered in Toronto, was organized April 22, 1919, covering eastern Canada.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Heber J. Grant opened the Japanese Mission in 1901; the first missionaries arrived at Yokohama on August 12, 1901.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: The Swedish Mission was formally established in July 1905 with Peter Matson as president.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: The Tongan Mission was organized in 1916, separate from the Samoan Mission.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: After legal recognition in Prague in 1928 and the 1929 dedication by Elder John A. Widtsoe, the Czechoslovak Mission was organized; it was publishing a periodical by February 1930.

answers.name: Norway
answers.fact: The Norwegian Mission was organized in 1920 when the Scandinavian Mission was divided.

prompts.display_text: Pin a West or Central African country where the first Latter-day Saint missionaries arrived between 1978 and 1989.
prompts.text_original: A West or Central African country where the first Latter-day Saint missionaries arrived between 1978 and 1989.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Ghana, Nigeria, D.R. Congo, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire, Sierra Leone, Cape Verde
prompts.summary: After the June 1978 revelation on the priesthood, senior couples reached Nigeria and Ghana within months, where congregations had been waiting for years. In the following decade missionaries entered Zaire (1986), Liberia and Cote d'Ivoire (1987), Sierra Leone (1988) and Cape Verde (1989).

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: Missionary couples Cannon and Mabey arrived on December 5, 1978.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: The same two senior couples arrived to begin missionary work on November 9, 1978.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: Barnard and Cherry Silver arrived in Abidjan on April 22, 1988 as the first Church representatives.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Ralph and Jean Hutchings, the first missionaries to Zaire, arrived in Kinshasa in February 1986.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: The first missionary couple assigned to Liberia arrived in Monrovia on July 3, 1987.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: The first missionaries assigned to Sierra Leone arrived in Freetown on May 7-8, 1988.

answers.name: Cabo Verde
answers.fact: The first missionaries arrived in Praia in March 1989.
